From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intro + candidate slots for Production Serving Lead

Thanks, Ava — copying the panel.

A few clarifications from the hiring manager side (my asks):

Panel composition:
- Hiring manager: Rafael Mendes (me) — systems + deployment ownership focus
- Bar-raiser: Markus Klein — evaluate cross-team impact and scale decisions
- Infra/Serving: Vanessa Ortiz — kernel/latency tradeoffs, batching/caching patterns
- Product/Behavioral: Marissa Cole — customer impact, rollout decisions

Interview shape (recommended):
- 30m screen (high-level fit + leadership signals)
- 75m technical deep-dive (split roughly into: 20m architecture walkthrough, 30m design + tradeoffs, 25m hands-on problem / followups)

Leveling expectations (what we should calibrate on):
- L5 (Senior): Owns a large serving surface, makes orthogonal tradeoffs, implements safe rollouts with some guidance.
- L6 (Principal): Defines system-wide patterns (e.g., KV cache strategies that reduce token cost by 30%), drives cross-org replatforms, influences product direction.

Interview focus areas (where I want clear signals):
- Real-world latency optimization stories (esp. tail latency)
- Decision process for model fallbacks / graceful degradation
- Caching strategies: prefix vs KV cache decisions, invalidation semantics
- Quantization/ops tradeoffs when under throughput pressure
- Leading cross-team incidents and postmortem actions

Debrief rhythm: short rubric + 10m synchronous debrief after candidate to capture signal while fresh. I'll attach a one-pager rubric (calibration notes).

Attachments: hm_calibration_notes_v1.pdf (stubs).

Thanks for the framing, Rafael — this looks good. Two small proposals:

1) Add an explicit "system tradeoff" question in the deep dive that forces a bounded numerical estimate (e.g., given a 2x throughput target with same hardware budget, what would you change and why?). Helps separate L5 vs L6 reasoning.

2) Let's do a 10–15 minute pre-panel sync (call) with the interviewers 30 minutes before the candidate so we:
   - align on the rubric anchors (one-sentence pass/fail signals)
   - surface any redlines (non-starters) up front

I can host the pre-panel sync and bring a 1-slide checklist. I'll add a calendar invite for 30 minutes before the first panel slot.

Markus
Markus Klein | Head of Serving Infrastructure
